john-kiriakou.body_append:
## 'The human rights guy'

On [The Jason Jones Show](/wiki/john-kiriakou) in March 2026, [John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou) said a Greek-American colleague in the CIA counter-terrorism centre — himself both an army brigadier general and a psychiatrist — warned him that behind his back colleagues were calling him *"the human rights guy."* Kiriakou answered *"I don't care, I've heard it, I don't care."* His colleague pressed him: *"you know that's not a compliment, right?"* Kiriakou's answer was *"I'm right, and they're wrong."* He read the moment as the point at which he understood he would have to fight the [enhanced-interrogation](/wiki/enhanced-interrogation) programme alone.<Cite t="09:52" /><Cite t="10:22" />

## The retired-deputy-director email

After Kiriakou's December 2007 ABC News interview confirming CIA [waterboarding](/wiki/waterboarding), a retired deputy director of the [CIA](/wiki/cia) — whom Kiriakou does not name — wrote to him privately. Kiriakou says he kept the email as a souvenir. It read: *"You've chosen a difficult path. I'm glad somebody did. I only wish that it had been me."* Kiriakou treats it as the moment he realised *"I wasn't alone"* — even if senior officers were not willing to say so publicly.<Cite t="11:55" /><Cite t="12:25" />

## Ellsberg's warning about whistleblower finances

A few days before Kiriakou reported to federal prison, [Daniel Ellsberg](/wiki/daniel-ellsberg) said something to him he says he has never forgotten: *"If there's one thing that is consistent across all whistleblowers, it's that we never make a financial comeback. Never."* Kiriakou's reaction, he says, was *"Dan, that won't be me"* — an intended defiance he says he has since spent nineteen years demonstrating.<Cite t="16:33" /><Cite t="17:04" /><Cite t="17:37" />

## The Abu Zubaydah 56-hour vigil

[John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou) says he sat with [Abu Zubaydah](/wiki/abu-zubaydah) for 56 consecutive hours, tying the prisoner to the bed not because Zubaydah — shot and nearly killed on capture — could physically escape but because Kiriakou was *"practically delirious from fatigue"* and was afraid he would fall asleep. Kiriakou says he told Zubaydah, sitting at the foot of the bed: *"I should hate you. I should want to kill you. And I don't. You're pathetic … you're the fearsome Al-Qaeda? You're what we're so terrified of?"* Zubaydah, he says, was only in his twenties.<Cite t="25:26" /><Cite t="25:57" />

## The prison chapel, the Ukrainian Orthodox cellmate, and the Johnstown priest

Sent to federal prison in 2013, [John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou) says he first worked in the prison library, then transferred to the chapel, which he preferred largely because he came to trust the chaplain — the only prison official he says he *"genuinely liked and respected."* He found the chapel library carried no Orthodox books and wrote to a priest in Johnstown, Pennsylvania, who began sending him volumes of Church Fathers, Desert Fathers, saint biographies, and a four-volume encyclopaedia of saints, along with the Orthodox Study Bible. The only other Orthodox prisoner in the facility, Kiriakou notes with a wince, was Ukrainian Orthodox and imprisoned as a pedophile; Kiriakou had *"a personal policy"* not to associate with him. He also observed of the chapel that it was, in practice, a daytime refuge for prisoners the general population would attack — pedophiles were beaten in their cells, in the television room and in the yard, so *"the only place they can go during the day is either the chapel or the library."*<Cite t="22:16" /><Cite t="22:48" /><Cite t="23:20" /><Cite t="23:51" /><Cite t="24:23" /><Cite t="24:54" />

## The cousin who imported cocaine

When a cousin cut ties with [John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou) after his 2013 conviction — telling him *"I can't talk to you any more, you brought shame to our family"* — Kiriakou's reply, on his own retelling, was: *"I brought shame to our family? You imported cocaine for the Colombians — and I brought shame to our family?"* He treats the exchange as an early lesson that the reputational fallout of whistleblowing surfaces which relationships were *"an illusion"* to begin with.<Cite t="14:29" /><Cite t="15:00" />

## Forgiving the man his ex-wife had left him for

Years after his 2018 divorce, [John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou) says, he sought out the man his ex-wife had become close to and telephoned him from that man's own country. *"Don't worry, I'm not here to harm you. I just wanted to tell you I've thought about this a lot, and I forgive you."* When the man answered *"really,"* Kiriakou answered *"really — you shouldn't have done what you did, that was wrong, but I forgive you."* Kiriakou notes he did not need the forgiveness to land: *"we forgive for ourselves."*<Cite t="26:58" /><Cite t="27:29" /><Cite t="28:00" />

## Kiriakou's 56-hour vigil (2002)

[John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou) has described sitting at the foot of [Abu Zubaydah](/wiki/abu-zubaydah)'s bed for 56 consecutive hours after his capture — a period Kiriakou says left him *"practically delirious from fatigue."* He tied Zubaydah to the bed not because Zubaydah — shot and nearly killed during the raid — could physically escape, but because Kiriakou was afraid he would fall asleep himself and lose custody. Kiriakou says he told the prisoner directly, in the chair he had pulled up to the foot of the bed: *"I should hate you. I should want to kill you. And I don't. You're pathetic. You're the fearsome Al-Qaeda? You're what we're so terrified of? You're pathetic."* Zubaydah was *"only in his twenties."*<Cite t="25:26" /><Cite t="25:57" />

ken-dilanian.body_append:
## Sending drafts to Langley before the editor (Kiriakou, 2026)

On The Jason Jones Show in March 2026, [John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou) said the investigative journalist [Jason Leopold](/wiki/jason-leopold) — labelled a *"FOIA terrorist"* by George W. Bush's Pentagon spokesman for the volume of his Freedom of Information Act filings — was bored one week between Christmas and New Year and filed a request for all correspondence between the [CIA](/wiki/cia) and American journalists over a two-year window. When the agency failed to respond within the sixty-day statutory deadline, Leopold's lawyer filed a federal suit on day 61 and won, forcing the release. Most of the correspondence was routine interview requests, but the finding that stood out, in Kiriakou's telling, concerned [Ken Dilanian](/wiki/ken-dilanian) — then NBC News's chief national-security correspondent — who was writing articles and *"sending them to the CIA for clearance before sending them to his own editor,"* asking *"is this okay, you guys? Are you cool with it? Cuz if you're not, just let me know and I'll take stuff out."*<Cite t="43:07" /><Cite t="43:38" /><Cite t="44:10" /><Cite t="44:43" />

jason-leopold.body_append:
## 'FOIA terrorist' and the CIA-journalist correspondence dump

[John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou) says [Jason Leopold](/wiki/jason-leopold) has filed *"more Freedom of Information Act requests than anybody else in the world"* — to the point that George W. Bush's Pentagon spokesman publicly labelled him a *"FOIA terrorist"* and, in Kiriakou's telling, threatened him over his use of the statute. Kiriakou says Leopold's practice is to file the request, wait sixty statutory days for a response, and file a federal suit on day 61 when — inevitably — none has arrived: *"He always wins, and the CIA always has to pay his legal fees."* Kiriakou attributes to Leopold both the breaking of the Hillary Clinton private-email-server story and the FOIA-driven exposure of [Ken Dilanian](/wiki/ken-dilanian)'s practice of sending drafts to the [CIA](/wiki/cia) before sending them to his own editor.<Cite t="42:37" /><Cite t="43:07" /><Cite t="43:38" /><Cite t="44:10" />

daniel-ellsberg.body_append:
## The pre-prison warning to Kiriakou

A few days before [John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou) reported to federal prison in 2013, [Daniel Ellsberg](/wiki/daniel-ellsberg) — whom Kiriakou calls the godfather of national-security whistleblowers — sat him down with a warning Kiriakou says he has never forgotten: *"If there's one thing that is consistent across all whistleblowers, it's that we never make a financial comeback. Never."* Kiriakou answered *"Dan, that won't be me"* — a defiance he says he has spent the years since attempting to make good on.<Cite t="16:33" /><Cite t="17:04" /><Cite t="17:37" /> Kiriakou notes that Ellsberg himself was never charged under the [Espionage Act](/wiki/espionage-act) because the Nixon administration's *"plumbers"* had burgled his psychiatrist's office and released his medical records to the press, tainting any prosecution.<Cite t="16:33" />

## 'Noted anti-semite' and the 2026 FARA referral

[John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou) has recounted a running private joke with [Tucker Carlson](/wiki/tucker-carlson) that turns on the shifting semantic weight of *"anti-semite"*: Kiriakou — described in a scholarly journal by the Israeli foreign minister's political director as *"noted anti-semite John Kiriakou"* — mentioned the label to Carlson, who topped it: *"that's nothing — I'm anti-semite of the year."* Kiriakou says the term *"used to mean you hated Jews"* and now *"means you refuse to hate Arabs or Muslims."*<Cite t="45:47" /><Cite t="46:19" /><Cite t="46:50" />

In March 2026, Kiriakou treated Carlson's [FARA referral](/wiki/tucker-carlson-2026-fara-referral) as legally weak — Carlson had *"great lawyers"* and did not fear prosecution — but singled out Ted Cruz and Lindsey Graham as *"dangerous tools of Israel"* and warned Carlson that the real risk was the [Charlie Kirk](/wiki/charlie-kirk-shooting) pattern of physical attack from *"a lot of crazy people out there."*<Cite t="46:50" /><Cite t="48:24" /><Cite t="48:56" />
